meta.purpose: Every irregularity and every value that could not be confirmed from an official source, with what was checked and where a reviewer can look. This page is the reason the merge is safe: nothing unverified is hidden in the site, it is published here instead.

severity_legend.high: affects whether the site can earn, or could mislead a reader
severity_legend.medium: limits a decision but does not break anything

flags.title: All five supplied codes are 9 characters, not valid ASINs
flags.what_we_saw: Each supplied link is of the form link.amazon/<9 characters>. Verified by counting the path segment of every supplied URL and comparing it with the ASIN definition Amazon publishes in its Catalog Items API reference, where the asin path parameter is 'The Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) of the item'. The four redirect targets that resolved are all 10 characters, which is consistent with an ASIN and inconsistent with the supplied slugs.
flags.why_it_matters: The supplied code is a short-link slug, not a product identifier. Anyone treating it as the ASIN will store the wrong value in a product record, and the confirmation record required by this project would then be wrong in a way that looks right.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Whether the owner intended these slugs to be ASINs. The record therefore carries intended_asin as blank for every row and keeps the observed redirect target in a separate field.
flags.review_action: Confirm the intended ASIN for each product in the Associates dashboard and enter it in intended_asin. Do not copy the slug into that field.

flags.title: No supplied link was observed to carry the tracking ID shopnow047c-20
flags.what_we_saw: Each link was requested and followed to its destination. None of the destination URLs visibly contained the tag parameter. The program requires the Associates ID to appear as a parameter in the URL of each link, in a form the policies write as XXXXX-##.
flags.why_it_matters: If the tag is not on the link, clicks may not be attributed, and no content on this site can fix that.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Whether the redirector attaches the tag server-side after a click. It could, and a browser fetch may not reveal the final tagged URL the way a signed-in click would.
flags.review_action: Click one link while signed in to the Associates dashboard and check whether the click appears under shopnow047c-20. One link, one product, before any scaling.

flags.title: Compliance status of the link.amazon short-link host is unresolved
flags.what_we_saw: The links redirect through a shortener. The program prohibits using a link shortening service in a manner that makes it unclear that the reader is linking to an Amazon site. A redirector that surfaces the Amazon destination is a different case from one that conceals it.
flags.why_it_matters: This determines whether the links can be used at all. It is deliberately left open rather than decided.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: The exact behaviour is only observable on click, and no official page addresses this host by name in a way that could be cited here. We are explicitly not claiming the links are invalid.
flags.review_action: Run the one-link test. If the destination is visibly Amazon and the click registers, record that as the measured result and date it.

flags.title: Commission rates are not published, because they sit behind a sign-in
flags.what_we_saw: The commission schedule URL resolves to an Associates sign-in page rather than a readable rate card.
flags.why_it_matters: Any revenue estimate would need a rate. Guessing one would put a fabricated number into a table that is supposed to be verified.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: The current rates for the relevant categories.
flags.review_action: Read the rate card while signed in. Until then the rate field stays blank on the site.

flags.title: One supplied link never resolved to a product
flags.what_we_saw: link.amazon/B0c8moW59 returned Amazon's /checkpoint/continue continue-shopping interstitial on every attempt, repeated across several minutes. The page is an official Amazon page, but it carries no product identity.
flags.why_it_matters: We cannot name the product, so we cannot describe it, and the site publishes no card and no outbound button for it. Publishing a button for an unidentified product would be the exact hallucination risk this project is guarding against.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: The product, its ASIN, and its category.
flags.review_action: Open the link in a normal browser, let the interstitial pass, and read the product name and ASIN from the page. Send both back and the row can be completed.

flags.title: No price, rating, review count or availability appears anywhere
flags.what_we_saw: Program Policies 2(b) permits price and availability display only where Amazon serves the link carrying it, or where it arrives via the Creators API or PA API. Neither condition holds here.
flags.why_it_matters: This is a rule, not an unfinished task. Filling the gap with a scraped or remembered figure would be a policy breach and a misrepresentation risk under the same section.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: n/a. The correct action is to leave it blank.
flags.review_action: If live figures are wanted, connect the API. Do not paste prices in manually.

flags.title: Product identity beyond brand, model and category is unverified
flags.what_we_saw: Wattage, dimensions, weight, warranty terms, energy use and noise are not stated in a citable official form for these units with the access available.
flags.why_it_matters: These are the numbers readers use to shortlist. Their absence limits the comparison page to form factor and stated claims.
flags.review_action: Supply figures from the manufacturer's own documentation, with a link, and they can be added as manufacturer-stated values.

flags.title: The repository contained no prior site
flags.what_we_saw: Git history holds one commit and one eight-byte README. There was no landing page, no dashboard, no data and no content to migrate or preserve.
flags.why_it_matters: The brief refers to an existing site that reads like generated content. That site is not in this repository, so nothing was removed. Any prior surface described elsewhere should be checked against that other location, not against this commit.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Where the prior site is deployed, if anywhere.
flags.source: repository git log at commit cca8c2a
flags.review_action: If a prior deployment exists elsewhere, point this project at it. Do not assume the deployed site matches this repo.

flags.title: Analytics is specified, not running
flags.what_we_saw: Five events are defined with a collector design. Nothing is deployed. The site loads no third-party script, sets no cookie, and writes nothing to storage.
flags.why_it_matters: A stated measurement plan that silently collects nothing would be worse than an honest blank, because it would make later decisions look data-driven when they are not.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Where the collector should run. GitHub Pages is static and cannot host a process.
flags.review_action: Choose a first-party host, or accept a third-party provider and add the disclosure it requires. Then deploy.

flags.title: The campaign ledger is empty and contains no forecast
flags.what_we_saw: The ledger ships with columns and zero rows. No conversion, revenue or projection figure is presented anywhere on the site.
flags.why_it_matters: A revenue forecast built on no orders is invented. The project brief asks for evidence-based iteration, which begins with an empty ledger.
flags.review_action: Add rows only from authorised reports, each with the date and the report name.

flags.title: Search Console verification and sitemap submission were not performed
flags.what_we_saw: Both require access to a Search Console account for the publishing domain. The sitemap, feed and robots.txt are generated and correct, but not yet submitted.
flags.why_it_matters: Until the sitemap is submitted, indexing depends on discovery rather than on being told.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Which domain will ultimately be canonical. The site currently canonicalises to the GitHub Pages URL of this repository.
flags.review_action: Verify the property, submit /sitemap.xml, and confirm the canonical host matches the domain actually used.

flags.title: No reader-capture mechanism was built
flags.what_we_saw: There is no email field, and deliberately so. A signup form without a provider, a consent record and an unsubscribe path is a compliance problem disguised as a feature.
flags.why_it_matters: The audience-building plan in the brief depends on this, so it is called out rather than quietly skipped.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Intended provider, consent language, and the legal sender identity.
flags.review_action: Choose a provider, write the consent and privacy language, then it can be built in an afternoon.

flags.title: No author identity is published, and no editorial titles are supported by query data
flags.what_we_saw: The four guides are published as hypotheses. No search-volume, popularity or superiority claim is made. There is no byline, because inventing a persona would be fabrication.
flags.why_it_matters: Both readers and search engines discount anonymous advice. An author page is the cheapest credibility upgrade available, and it is blocked on a real name.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: The publishing name, the author's background, and whether the site tests products.
flags.review_action: Supply a name and a two-sentence bio. Then publish the byline and the author page.

flags.title: Five supplied links, four identified products
flags.what_we_saw: Four of the five resolved to identifiable Amazon listings. The fifth returned only a bot check. The site therefore presents four products and states plainly that a fifth was supplied and could not be identified.
flags.why_it_matters: Silently dropping it would misrepresent the brief; inventing it would be worse. Publishing the gap is the only honest option.
flags.review_action: Open it in a browser and report the product name and ASIN. The site is built so that adding the row is a data edit, not a rebuild.

flags.title: No product photography is used
flags.what_we_saw: Amazon-served imagery is Program Content, which may not be altered, and using a stock photograph of a different appliance would misrepresent the product.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest gap between the current design and a typical polished retail page. It is a licensing and consent gap, not a design one.
flags.what_we_could_not_determine: Whether the account has API access that would permit unmodified image fields.
flags.review_action: Enrol the Creators API or PA API, or use Amazon-served link formats that carry the image. Then the gallery can be built without touching stock photography.
